headline: Habagat Rains Prompt Monday Class Suspensions in Parts of Northern and Western Luzon
seoTitle: Habagat Rains Prompt August 24 Class Suspensions | FMB News
seoDescription: Heavy southwest monsoon rains prompted preemptive class suspensions in parts of Northern and Western Luzon for Monday, August 24, 2026.
deck: Heavy southwest monsoon rains and saturated ground conditions prompted precautionary school suspensions in vulnerable Luzon communities ahead of Monday classes.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA warned Sunday evening of continued southwest monsoon rains over parts of Luzon, with local governments in vulnerable northern and western areas announcing precautionary class suspensions for Monday, August 24.

The approved FMB News brief cited landslide and road-clearing concerns in Batanes and continuing rain risk in western Luzon. Suspension decisions remain local, so students and parents should follow their city, municipality or school division for the final list.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: PAGASA forecasts have shown unsettled monsoon weather over western and northern parts of the country through the weekend, with saturated ground increasing the risk of localized flooding and landslides.
The newsroom brief attributes the Sunday evening advisory and local suspension notices to PAGASA, civil-defense authorities and local governments.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Localized suspension reporting needs geographic precision. A suspension in one municipality does not automatically apply to an entire province, and conditions can change overnight.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Residents should check the latest PAGASA rainfall warnings, local disaster-office advisories and official LGU or DepEd announcements before traveling to school or work Monday morning.
